claims.text: Grain size governs the magnetocaloric response and hysteresis of as-deposited, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type high-entropy alloys.
Phase distribution governs the magnetocaloric response and hysteresis of these alloys.
Magnetic-field-induced changes in magnetic anisotropy govern the magnetocaloric response and hysteresis of these alloys.
The governing behavior arises from interplay between microstructural features and field-induced changes in magnetic anisotropy.
Controlled annealing will modify grain size and phase distribution.
Optimizing microstructural features by annealing will improve the magnetocaloric response relative to the as-deposited baseline.
Optimizing microstructural features by annealing will reduce hysteresis relative to the as-deposited baseline.
The predictions apply only over annealing temperatures and times that retain mechanical stability.
The proposed comparison is between as-deposited and annealed alloys under low-applied-field magnetic-cooling conditions.
Magnetization-versus-temperature curves and hysteresis loops can be used to compare magnetocaloric response and hysteresis.
No improvement in magnetocaloric response after annealing would falsify the hypothesis.
Increased hysteresis after annealing would falsify the hypothesis.
